title: cluster got into an unrecoverable state after deleting and recreating a collection
body:
## Current Behavior
Calls to, scroll, insert points, create collections and delete collections start to timeout. After a little bit all calls start 500ing with ` too many replicas returned an error` Errors from logs in detailed description.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Have a couple collections loaded with 10k+ points each
2. Have 4 nodes in cluster configuration
3. Delete collections
4. Create collections with same name
5. Start reinserting points*
\* we insert about 25 points per call. concurrently between multiple application servers. 

## Expected Behavior
I should be able to delete and recreate indexes without consensus algorithm putting cluster into a unrecoverable state.

## Possible Solution
This isnt a fix but as a work around Im going to rewrite the index rebuild to create a new collection and cut over to it. Its a better implementation but was trying to avoid versioning collections.

How we recovered from this incident was uninstalling the helm application, removing the persistent volume claims, installing the helm application. Then updating running application server to point at the new empty cluster. Rebuild each collection one at a time. 😢 

## Context (Environment)
Our application workflow is primarily search based. The search cluster returning no data or timing out means that we had a site wide outage for about an hour.

Qdrant 1.1.0, 4x nodes in kube.
collections
shard 8
replication_factor 2


## Detailed Description
```
[2023-04-04T18:15:50.080Z WARN  storage::content_manager::consensus_manager] Failed to apply collection meta operation entry with user error: Wrong input: Replica 6850656706223262058 of shard 0 has state Some(Active), but expected Some(Initializing)

[2023-04-04T18:13:59.822Z WARN  storage::content_manager::consensus_manager] Failed to send message to http://qdrant-1.qdrant-headless:6335/ with error: Error in closure supplied to transport channel pool: status: DeadlineExceeded, message: "Timeout exceeded", details: [], metadata: MetadataMap { headers: {} }

[2023-04-04T18:11:10.294Z ERROR qdrant::consensus] Failed to propose entry: ProposalDropped

[2023-04-04T18:11:05.969Z WARN  collection::shards::replica_set] Failed to update shard COLLECTION_NAME:1 on peer 14108870475277683833, error: Service internal error: Tonic status error: The operation was cancelled

[2023-04-04T18:18:53.194Z WARN  qdrant::actix::helpers] error processing request: Waiting for consensus operation commit failed. Timeout set at: 10 seconds 
```

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: Bumping this. If we do it for a single collection, we also hit the same error here. I think issuing a delete right after collection creation causes this issue, in a cluster mode.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
I did some basic testing with concurrent creation and deletion of collection and I was unfortunately not able to reproduce this issue.

@participant1 Can you please share as well some information about your setup?

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
I wonder if the underlying filesystem could be the problem.

Or if this is on macOS (I don't think so), we might flush incorrectly:

> For applications that require tighter guarantees about the integrity of
their data, Mac OS X provides the F_FULLFSYNC fcntl. The F_FULLFSYNC
fcntl asks the drive to flush all buffered data to permanent storage.
Applications, such as databases, that require a strict ordering of writes
should use F_FULLFSYNC to ensure that their data is written in the order
they expect. ([ref](https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/System/Conceptual/ManPages_iPhoneOS/man2/fsync.2.html))

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
@participant3 

I have the same issue again today. It seems like one single node corrupt the whole cluster. I was creating a index with 1 shard & replication factor of 1, and this issue appears. 

We are running in a 5 node setup on Kubernetes, backed by GP2 EBS volume.

This issue appears in one of the cluster health check test we implemented. This test does exactly 4 things using REST API:

- Creating a index called `collection_creation_test`
- Checking against "List collections" REST endpoint & see if the newly created index is there
- Checking against "Collection info" REST endpoint & see if there are any errors given -> this is where it fails
  - Error message: `[2023-08-14T16:52:36.489Z WARN  qdrant::actix::helpers] error processing request: The replica set for shard 0 on peer 2077498272239626 has no active replica
`
- Dropping the index called `collection_creation_test`

The above sequence is running okay for 1 week and all of a sudden on the weekend it started to fail.

Once it failed for the first time, there is no way to recover it unless:
 - Dropping the persistent volume & the data for the entire cluster

Probably worth replicating this issue using a script. Basically does the above 3 things & see if it will fail.

>  wonder if the underlying filesystem could be the problem.

We are using a GP2 volume on AWS, so it is very unlikely that the file system is the issue here.

comments.body:
Hi. I've ran into a similar issue with an unrecoverable state, where one of the nodes got stuck on an older commit and is causing issues. 

I can reproduce it fairly reliably by introducing 10s latency on one node (using a `tc` tool) for a while and then removing the extra latency.

The cluster is running on version 1.4.1.

The end state is:

Running `curl "${URL}/cluster" ${CURL_FLAGS} | jq -c '{"url":<nick>URL ,"status":.status, "raft_info": .result.raft_info}'` shows:

```json
{"url":"http://localhost:6333","status":"ok","raft_info":{"term":115,"commit":150,"pending_operations":0,"leader":3413489478446639,"role":"Follower","is_voter":<nick>}}
{"url":"http://localhost:6343","status":"ok","raft_info":{"term":115,"commit":223,"pending_operations":0,"leader":3413489478446639,"role":"Follower","is_voter":<nick>}}
{"url":"http://localhost:6353","status":"ok","raft_info":{"term":115,"commit":223,"pending_operations":0,"leader":3413489478446639,"role":"Leader","is_voter":<nick>}}
```

Running `curl ${URL}/collections/test_collection` on each node results in 2 out of 3 returning errors:

```json
{"result":{"status":"green","optimizer_status":"ok","vectors_count":6,"indexed_vectors_count":0,"points_count":6,"segments_count":6,"config":{"params":{"vectors":{"size":4,"distance":"Dot"},"shard_number":3,"replication_factor":1,"write_consistency_factor":1,"on_disk_payload":<nick>},"hnsw_config":{"m":16,"ef_construct":100,"full_scan_threshold":10000,"max_indexing_threads":0,"on_disk":<nick>},"optimizer_config":{"deleted_threshold":0.2,"vacuum_min_vector_number":1000,"default_segment_number":0,"max_segment_size":<nick>,"memmap_threshold":<nick>,"indexing_threshold":20000,"flush_interval_sec":5,"max_optimization_threads":1},"wal_config":{"wal_capacity_mb":32,"wal_segments_ahead":0},"quantization_config":<nick>},"payload_schema":{}},"status":"ok","time":0.030598695}
{"status":{"error":"Service internal error: The replica set for shard 1 on peer 8458440906768741 has no active replica"},"time":0.029179821}
{"status":{"error":"Service internal error: The replica set for shard 1 on peer 3413489478446639 has no active replica"},"time":0.000127621}
```

I didn't know how to reproduce it as python test, so I've wrote a `docker-compose.yaml` and a bash script that should let you reproduce a cluster in a broken state.

To reproduce:

1. make a `Dockerfile` with `qdrant` and `tc` tool from `iproute2` package:

```dockerfile
FROM qdrant/qdrant:latest
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y iproute2
```

2. make a `docker-compose.yaml` with 3 nodes. Based on `tools/generate_docker_compose_cluster.sh` with addition of `tc` command.

```docker-compose
version: "3.7"

services:
  qdrant_node_0:
    container_name: node0
    build: .
    command: bash -c "tc qdisc add dev eth0 root netem delay 10ms && ./qdrant --uri 'http://qdrant_node_0:6335'"
    restart: always
    cap_add:
      - NET_ADMIN
    environment:
      - QDRANT__SERVICE__GRPC_PORT=6334
      - QDRANT__CLUSTER__ENABLED=true
      - QDRANT__CLUSTER__P2P__PORT=6335
      - QDRANT__CLUSTER__CONSENSUS__MAX_MESSAGE_QUEUE_SIZE=5000
      - QDRANT__LOG_LEVEL=debug,raft=info
    ports:
      - "6333:6333"
      - "6334:6334"
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: "0.3"

  qdrant_node_1:
    container_name: node1
    build: .
    command: bash -c "tc qdisc add dev eth0 root netem delay 10ms && sleep 5 && ./qdrant --bootstrap 'http://qdrant_node_0:6335' --uri 'http://qdrant_node_1:6335'"
    restart: always
    cap_add:
      - NET_ADMIN
    environment:
      - QDRANT__SERVICE__GRPC_PORT=6334
      - QDRANT__CLUSTER__ENABLED=true
      - QDRANT__CLUSTER__P2P__PORT=6335
      - QDRANT__CLUSTER__CONSENSUS__MAX_MESSAGE_QUEUE_SIZE=5000
      - QDRANT__LOG_LEVEL=debug,raft=info
    ports:
      - "6343:6333"
      - "6344:6334"
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: "0.3"

  qdrant_node_2:
    container_name: node2
    build: .
    command: bash -c "tc qdisc add dev eth0 root netem delay 10ms && sleep 10 && ./qdrant --bootstrap 'http://qdrant_node_0:6335' --uri 'http://qdrant_node_2:6335'"
    restart: always
    cap_add:
      - NET_ADMIN
    environment:
      - QDRANT__SERVICE__GRPC_PORT=6334
      - QDRANT__CLUSTER__ENABLED=true
      - QDRANT__CLUSTER__P2P__PORT=6335
      - QDRANT__CLUSTER__CONSENSUS__MAX_MESSAGE_QUEUE_SIZE=5000
      - QDRANT__LOG_LEVEL=debug,raft=info
    ports:
      - "6353:6333"
      - "6354:6334"
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: "0.3"

```

3. make a `test.sh` bash script to reproduce the issue. The API calls are mostly taken from `QUICK_START.md`

```bash
#!/bin/bash

PORTS=( 6333 6343 6353 )
CURL_FLAGS="--silent --show-error"

# Array of all URLs
URLS=()
for PORT in ${PORTS[@]}; do
    URLS+=( "http://localhost:${PORT}" )
done

function random_url () {
    R=RANDOM%${#URLS[@]}
    echo ${URLS[$R]}
}

function delete_collection () {
    echo "Delete collection"
    export URL=`random_url` 
    curl -X DELETE "${URL}/collections/test_collection" \
        ${CURL_FLAGS} \
    | jq -c '{"url":<nick>URL ,"status":.status}'
}

function create_collection () {
    echo "Create collection"
    export URL=`random_url` 
    curl -X PUT "${URL}/collections/test_collection" \
        -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
        --data-raw '{
            "vectors": {
            "size": 4,
            "distance": "Dot"
            },
            "shard_number":3,
            "replication_factor":1
        }' \
        ${CURL_FLAGS} \
    | jq -c '{"url":<nick>URL ,"status":.status}'
}

function get_collection () {
    echo "Get collection"
    export URL=`random_url` 
    curl "${URL}/collections/test_collection" \
        ${CURL_FLAGS} \
    | jq -c '{"url":<nick>URL ,"status":.status}'
}

function insert_points () {
    echo "Insert points"
    export URL=`random_url` 
    curl -L -X PUT "${URL}/collections/test_collection/points?wait=true" \
        -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
        --data-raw '{
            "points": [
            {"id": 1, "vector": [0.05, 0.61, 0.76, 0.74], "payload": {"city": "Berlin"}},
            {"id": 2, "vector": [0.19, 0.81, 0.75, 0.11], "payload": {"city": ["Berlin", "London"] }},
            {"id": 3, "vector": [0.36, 0.55, 0.47, 0.94], "payload": {"city": ["Berlin", "Moscow"] }},
            {"id": 4, "vector": [0.18, 0.01, 0.85, 0.80], "payload": {"city": ["London", "Moscow"] }},
            {"id": 5, "vector": [0.24, 0.18, 0.22, 0.44], "payload": {"count": [0] }},
            {"id": 6, "vector": [0.35, 0.08, 0.11, 0.44]}
            ]
        }'\
        ${CURL_FLAGS} \
    | jq -c '{"url":<nick>URL ,"status":.status}'
}

function search_points() {
    echo "Search points"
    export URL=`random_url` 
    curl -L -X POST "${URL}/collections/test_collection/points/search" \
        -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
        --data-raw '{
            "vector": [0.2,0.1,0.9,0.7],
            "top": 3
        }' \
        ${CURL_FLAGS} \
    | jq -c '{"url":<nick>URL ,"status":.status}'
}

function check_raft {
    echo "Check raft"
    for URL in ${URLS[@]}; do   
        export URL=${URL} 
        curl "${URL}/cluster" \
            ${CURL_FLAGS} \
        | jq -c '{"url":<nick>URL ,"status":.status, "raft_info": .result.raft_info}'
    done
}

function check_collection {
    echo "Check collection"
    for URL in ${URLS[@]}; do   
        export URL=${URL} 
        curl "${URL}/collections/test_collection" \
            ${CURL_FLAGS} \
        | jq -c '{"url":<nick>URL ,"status":.status, "raft_info": .result.raft_info}'
    done
}


function change_latency () {
    NODE=$1
    LATENCY=$2
    docker exec ${NODE} tc qdisc change dev eth0 root netem delay ${LATENCY}
    echo "Running with ${LATENCY} latency on ${NODE}"
}

function run_tests () {
    # Iterations counter is $1 arg, or `1` if not set
    ITERATIONS=${1:-1}
    for x in $(seq 1 $ITERATIONS); do
        delete_collection
        create_collection
        delete_collection
        create_collection
        insert_points
        search_points
        echo "raft_status after $x iterations:"
        check_raft
    done

}

# Check initial state of raft
check_raft

# Simulate reasonable latency
change_latency node0 10ms
change_latency node1 10ms
change_latency node2 10ms

# Some warmup in reasonable conditions
run_tests 10

# Simulate extremely bad latency on node0
change_latency node0 10000ms

# Run enough tests for 
run_tests 3

# Return node0 to reasonable latency
change_latency node0 10ms

# Run some tests after the "network issue"
run_tests 10

# Now I can see that node0 got stuck on an old commit
# {"url":"http://localhost:6333","status":"ok","raft_info":{"term":115,"commit":150,"pending_operations":0,"leader":3413489478446639,"role":"Follower","is_voter":<nick>}}
# {"url":"http://localhost:6343","status":"ok","raft_info":{"term":115,"commit":223,"pending_operations":0,"leader":3413489478446639,"role":"Follower","is_voter":<nick>}}
# {"url":"http://localhost:6353","status":"ok","raft_info":{"term":115,"commit":223,"pending_operations":0,"leader":3413489478446639,"role":"Leader","is_voter":<nick>}}

# Getting a collection fails on node1 and node2
check_collection

# {"result":{"status":"green","optimizer_status":"ok","vectors_count":6,"indexed_vectors_count":0,"points_count":6,"segments_count":6,"config":{"params":{"vectors":{"size":4,"distance":"Dot"},"shard_number":3,"replication_factor":1,"write_consistency_factor":1,"on_disk_payload":<nick>},"hnsw_config":{"m":16,"ef_construct":100,"full_scan_threshold":10000,"max_indexing_threads":0,"on_disk":<nick>},"optimizer_config":{"deleted_threshold":0.2,"vacuum_min_vector_number":1000,"default_segment_number":0,"max_segment_size":<nick>,"memmap_threshold":<nick>,"indexing_threshold":20000,"flush_interval_sec":5,"max_optimization_threads":1},"wal_config":{"wal_capacity_mb":32,"wal_segments_ahead":0},"quantization_config":<nick>},"payload_schema":{}},"status":"ok","time":0.030598695}
# {"status":{"error":"Service internal error: The replica set for shard 1 on peer 8458440906768741 has no active replica"},"time":0.029179821}
# {"status":{"error":"Service internal error: The replica set for shard 1 on peer 3413489478446639 has no active replica"},"time":0.000127621}
```

4. Run the tests
```bash
chmod +x test.sh
docker-compose up -d && sleep 15 && ./test.sh | tee test.log
```

comments.body:
The missing debug logs might be because of `slog` disables trace and debug logs in release builds. See [notice](https://docs.rs/slog/latest/slog/#notable-details)

`Note: At compile time slog by default removes trace and debug level statements in release builds, and trace level records in debug builds. This makes trace and debug level logging records practically free, which should encourage using them freely. If you want to enable trace/debug messages or raise the compile time logging level limit, use the following in your Cargo.toml:`

```
slog = { version = ... ,
         features = ["max_level_trace", "release_max_level_warn"] }
```

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
@participant5 I think I was able to fix it based on my previous observation.

I stumbled upon the same panic while writing my unit test :<nick>: 

https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/pull/2508

The fact that the team is not able to reproduce it with an integration test is still a mystery.

comments.author: participant5
comments.body:
Ah, I've switched to the dev build for that one, so the debug_asserts kicked in.

I see there's a possible fix coming on the branch. I'll check if I can reproduce the issue with that branch.

comments.author: participant6
comments.body: @participant2 @participant5 I've (finally) managed to reproduce the issue on current `dev`, and just re-run the test with the fix from #2508. There's a `found conflict at index ...` line in the logs, but the issue _did not_ reproduce with the fix.

comments.author: participant5
comments.body: I'm running the test case in a loop while I'm not at my laptop. I'll let you know if the issue is gone when I'm back.

comments.author: participant5
comments.body:
Ok, I've got 15 runs in a row without the issue. I think it's safe to assume the PR fixes the issue.

Update: 100 runs completed successfully in the meantime. 

I'll run the same test loop with 2 and 3 nodes experiencing the "network issue" and maybe with a 5-node cluster, just to see if the cluster still recovers in different setups.

I haven't found any other issues with more tests. 

Is there an ETA on when #2508 gets merged into master and released? This issue is a blocker for me, as it happens quite often in my setup.

Hi @participant5. It took us a bit longer, sorry about that.

But here's the good news; we've just released [v1.5.0](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/releases/tag/v1.5.0). It includes <https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/pull/2508> which is what you're looking for. :<nick>: 

Since I believe this is resolved with this update, I'll close this now.
